title: System Design
author: Charikshith
description: A full system-design course — fundamentals (networking, protocols, architecture, scalability, storage, performance, reliability, security) through end-to-end designs of real systems like TinyURL, YouTube, Uber, and Google Drive. Diagram-heavy.
tagline: From basics to cracking interviews — a complete journey through networking, scalability, storage, performance, security, and 8 real-world case studies.
intro: Whether you're new to system design or preparing for tough interviews, this course gives you the structured thinking to design robust, scalable systems — for real-world impact, not just whiteboarding.
learn: Reason about latency, throughput, and trade-offs intuitively
Apply the 4-step design framework to any problem
Choose between monolith, microservices, or event-driven
Design real systems: YouTube, Uber, Google Docs, and more
Recognize anti-patterns before they cost you

Introduction.summary: What system design is, why it matters, the 4-step framework, latency numbers every programmer should know, and common anti-patterns.
Introduction.subtitle: Whether you're new to system design or preparing for tough interviews, this guide builds a rock-solid foundation and gives you the tools to design robust, scalable systems — for real-world impact, not just whiteboarding.

Networking & Communication.summary: IP, DNS, proxies, load balancers, API gateways, CDNs, and the canonical "what happens when you type google.com" trace.
Networking & Communication.subtitle: Networking is the backbone of every large-scale system. This chapter walks through IP addresses, DNS, the client-server model, proxies, load balancers, API gateways, and CDNs — the building blocks that move bytes between every component you'll ever design.

Protocols (System Design Fundamentals).summary: UDP, TCP, HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3, REST, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSockets, Server-Sent Events — how clients and servers actually talk.
Protocols (System Design Fundamentals).subtitle: From TCP's reliable handshakes to HTTP/3 over QUIC, from REST's CRUD verbs to WebSockets, SSE, gRPC streams and GraphQL queries — protocols decide how every byte travels. This chapter is the practical, interview-ready tour you'll keep coming back to.

Architectural Patterns (System Design Fu.summary: Monolith, modular monolith, microservices, event-driven, BFF, CQRS, Event Sourcing, Saga — and when NOT to use microservices.
Architectural Patterns (System Design Fu.subtitle: From the humble monolith to microservices, event-driven systems, and patterns like BFF, CQRS, and Saga — learn which architecture fits which problem, and how to evolve a system as it grows.

Web Concepts in System Design (System De.summary: Sessions, cookies, JWT, CORS, security headers, OAuth flows, the modern BFF + HttpOnly cookie pattern, and XSS/CSRF defense.
Web Concepts in System Design (System De.subtitle: From sessions, cookies, and JWT to CORS, security headers, OAuth, and the modern BFF authentication pattern — master the web fundamentals that power scalable, efficient, and secure applications.

Scalability in System Design.summary: Horizontal vs vertical, Amdahl's Law, USL, stateless design, circuit breakers, bulkheads, rate limiting, backpressure, capacity planning.
Scalability in System Design.subtitle: Vertical, horizontal, and diagonal scaling; load balancing, autoscaling, and Amdahl's Law; circuit breakers, bulkheads, and rate limiting — everything you need to grow a system from 1,000 to 1 billion users without it falling over.

Storage - Database and Storage.summary: SQL vs NoSQL, CAP theorem, sharding, replication, B-Tree vs LSM-Tree, consistency spectrum, specialized DBs (time-series, vector, graph).
Storage - Database and Storage.subtitle: Master the storage layer of modern systems — SQL vs. NoSQL trade-offs, the CAP theorem during partitions, sharding and replication strategies, B-Tree vs. LSM-Tree engines, and when to reach for object, file, block, or specialized databases.

Performance - Concepts, Tools & Techniqu.summary: Caching patterns (5 of them), cache stampede, N+1 query, message queues, indexing, query optimization, concurrency vs parallelism.
Performance - Concepts, Tools & Techniqu.subtitle: Master the levers that make systems feel fast: caching strategies, message queues for decoupling, concurrency models, database indexing and query tuning — plus the anti-patterns (N+1 queries, cache stampedes, blocking I/O) that quietly destroy production performance.

Reliability, Availability & Disaster Rec.summary: 9s of availability, retry-with-backoff, idempotency keys, active-active vs active-passive, RTO/RPO, chaos engineering.
Reliability, Availability & Disaster Rec.subtitle: From the nine 9s of availability and retry-with-backoff to idempotency keys, active-active vs active-passive topologies, chaos engineering, and RTO/RPO — the patterns that keep modern systems standing when things go wrong.

Security in System Design – Principles,.summary: CIA triad, STRIDE, OAuth 2.0 flows, JWT pitfalls, defense-in-depth, encryption, secrets management, Zero Trust.
Security in System Design – Principles,.subtitle: Security is a core pillar — not a feature. This chapter walks through the CIA triad, threat modeling, OAuth 2.0 flows, JWT pitfalls, encryption & PKI, network segmentation, Zero Trust, defense-in-depth, OWASP Top 10, and the security headers every app should set by default.

The System Design Blueprint.summary: The 4-step methodology, interview frameworks (RADIO, REACTO), managing 45 minutes, reading the interviewer.
The System Design Blueprint.subtitle: The capstone of the foundational chapters — a proven 4-step methodology, time-management tactics for the 45-minute interview, and the interview frameworks (RADIO, REACTO) you'll lean on for every case study that follows.

Design a URL Shortener (TinyURL).summary: bit.ly clone — base62 encoding, key generation, caching, custom aliases, abuse prevention, click analytics.
Design a URL Shortener (TinyURL).subtitle: A complete bit.ly-style case study: from extreme read-write asymmetry and base62 encoding to Zookeeper-coordinated ID generation, hot-URL caching, custom aliases, and abuse prevention — applying the 4-step blueprint end-to-end.

Design an Auction Platform (aka eBay).summary: Concurrent bidding, anti-sniping extension, search/discovery, reviews, dispute resolution, multi-warehouse inventory.
Design an Auction Platform (aka eBay).subtitle: A fascinating challenge that touches latency, concurrency, real-time fan-out, and user trust — we'll architect a scalable, fair, and real-time auction platform that handles last-second bid storms, anti-sniping extensions, payments, and search.

Design a Cloud Storage Solution (aka Goo.summary: Chunking, block-level dedup, sync, sharing graph (Zanzibar), offline editing, conflict resolution (LWW vs three-way merge).
Design a Cloud Storage Solution (aka Goo.subtitle: Build a Drive- or Dropbox-class platform: chunked resumable uploads, block-level deduplication, real-time multi-device sync, fine-grained sharing, and conflict resolution at petabyte scale.

Design a Video Sharing Platform (aka You.summary: Transcoding pipeline, HLS/DASH adaptive streaming, view counter at scale, recommendations, Content ID, VOD vs Live.
Design a Video Sharing Platform (aka You.subtitle: Walk through the end-to-end architecture of a modern video platform — chunked uploads, a multi-resolution encoding pipeline, global CDN delivery, HLS/DASH adaptive streaming, sharded view counters, and a two-stage recommendation engine.

Design a Search Engine(aka Google).summary: Crawling, inverted index, TF-IDF, PageRank, query understanding, autocomplete, lexical vs semantic search.
Design a Search Engine(aka Google).subtitle: From distributed crawling and inverted indexes to PageRank, query understanding, autocomplete, and learned ranking — this case study walks through architecting a web-scale search engine that serves billions of pages in under 200 ms.

Design an E-Commerce Platform(aka Amazon.summary: Catalog, cart, checkout Saga, multi-warehouse inventory, faceted search, recommendations, returns workflow, fraud detection.
Design an E-Commerce Platform(aka Amazon.subtitle: Architect a high-scale multi-vendor marketplace like Amazon — from catalog and cart to a checkout Saga, multi-warehouse inventory, recommendations, and real-time fraud detection — without a distributed transaction in sight.

Design a Taxi Hailing App (aka Uber).summary: Geohash/S2/H3 spatial indexing, driver matching, surge pricing, ETA prediction, real-time location, fraud detection.
Design a Taxi Hailing App (aka Uber).subtitle: Geospatial matching with H3/geohash, surge pricing as a near-real-time supply/demand signal, ETA prediction beyond Haversine, live location streaming, and fraud detection — the full stack of a real-time, two-sided marketplace at planet scale.

Design a Collaborative Document Editor (.summary: Operational Transformation vs CRDTs, real-time presence, offline editing, comments anchoring, WebSocket fan-out.
Design a Collaborative Document Editor (.subtitle: Build a real-time multi-user editor like Google Docs — from OT vs CRDT conflict resolution and WebSocket fan-out to presence, offline editing, comments, and revision history. A case study in distributed concurrency under millisecond latency.

Final Prep, Mindset & Moving Forward.summary: Interview formats at top companies, what L4/L5/L6/L7 candidates do differently, when you get stuck, mock interview resources.
Final Prep, Mindset & Moving Forward.subtitle: The closing chapter of your system design journey — interview mindset, the repeatable 4-step framework, how top companies evaluate candidates, mock interview tactics, and how to keep growing as a system thinker after the offer.

Resources.summary: Videos and channels worth following once the course is done.
